To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

idioms are a special case of construction, that the use of constructions can be accounted for by a principle of self organization, and that the linguistic system as an entity can be fruitfully analyzed from a dynamic systems perspective.

(i) the patterns of stability/variation in the occurrence of idioms are accounted for in dynamic terms; (ii) the use of idioms is governed by a circular principle of causation; (iii) similar mechanisms may regulate linguistic variation in general.

(a) idioms are a subset of constructions that display a stable attractor state in their use; (b) the stable attractor state of an idiom is the result of an ongoing, nonlinear, self-organizing process that shapes the idiom as a whole; and (c) idioms are part of a larger system of constructions that is also governed by a principle similar to (b).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether and how idiomatic constructions can be fruitfully investigated from a dynamic systems perspective.
how the linguistic system is structured, how it is organized, and how it is used.
the emergence of idiomatic constructions, and the emergence of the linguistic system itself, as an outcome of the self organizing dynamics of a construction network.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
language is a dynamic, self-organizing system, whose functioning is regulated by a principle of circular causality.
language is a construction network, where each construction is an attractor state that constrains the possible occurrence of other constructions in a nonlinear and dynamic fashion.

idioms are emergent construction networks, and the language system is an emergent network of construction networks.
Language as an Emergence Construction Network: A
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
language as a whole can be described in terms of an emergent construction system.
language as a whole is an emergent construction network.
language is not a static system, but rather a dynamic system that emerges from the interactions between the elements of which it is made up.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the constructionist approach to language is not incompatible with a dynamic view of linguistic systems.
the constructionist approach is not only a useful framework for the analysis of language, but it also offers a powerful tool to investigate the dynamics of the language system.
the study of idioms can shed light on the dynamics of the linguistic system and, in general, on the nature of the language system as an emergent construction network.
